summary: Harmonies is a relaxed, colorful tile-stacking puzzle where you build small landscapes on a hex board to form habitats and settle animals onto them for points. It's mostly a personal, parallel puzzle with only light competition over the shared pool of tokens and animal cards.
praised: easy to teach and quick to play
satisfying puzzle with meaningful spatial choices
works well solo and at all player counts
criticised: light player interaction can feel too solitary for gamers wanting conflict
limited strategic depth for heavier-game fans
can feel samey across repeated plays
animal card draws add some luck

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light drafting
interaction.detail: Players choose token sets and animal cards from a small shared display, so timing what you take can deny others their preferred pick, but each player builds and scores their own landscape board entirely independently.

scoring.why: Nearly every terrain type has its own scoring rule (water, fields, forest, mountains, buildings/moon), on top of separate animal habitat cards, so almost every placement scores something.
scoring.how_you_win: You draft terrain tokens to build patterns matching multiple scoring shapes and settle animals into completed habitats, winning by having the highest sum across all these terrain and animal categories.
